title.narrative: 48hrs 3rd Envelope Emergency Response Plan for Syria: Rapid Health Services, Hygiene, and Essential Aid Deployment

description.narrative: ltpgtSARC is leading a critical humanitarian response to the 2025 wildfires in Latakia Governorate, focusing on Food Security, Non-Food Items (NFIs), Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), and Health (Medical Services) to assist 25,000 affected individuals. The wildfires have devastated agricultural land, destroyed livelihoods, and disrupted access to basic services, leaving communities in urgent need of support. For Food Security, SARC is distributing ready-to-eat meals and dry food parcels to displaced families and host communities, while also implementing multi-purpose cash assistance programs to help 5,000 households meet their immediate needs and stimulate local markets. Agricultural recovery efforts, including the provision of seeds, tools, and livestock feed, aim to restore food production and long-term resilience. In the NFIs sector, emergency shelter supplies such as hygiene kits, cooking sets, bedding, and winterization items (thermal blankets, heating stoves) are being distributed to over 2,000 displaced individuals, with a focus on vulnerable groups like female-headed households, the elderly, and persons with disabilities. WASH interventions are addressing the severe damage to water infrastructure, with emergency water trucking (960 cubic meters delivered) and bottled water distributions (4,050 bottles) ensuring safe drinking water, while hygiene promotion campaigns mitigate the risk of waterborne diseases. Rehabilitation of water pipelines and pumping stations (e.g., Al-Zour, Ballouran) is underway to restore sustainable access. In Health, Mobile Health Units (MHUs) are providing primary healthcare, treating smoke-related respiratory illnesses (26 cases) and trauma injuries (4 cases), while Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) services, including Psychological First Aid (PFA), are being offered to affected families and responders. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is being distributed to volunteers and health workers to safeguard against smoke exposure. Cross-sector coordination ensures integrated assistance, such as linking WASH and Health to prevent disease outbreaks, and combining NFIs with protection services to address gender-specific needs. Despite challenges like access constraints due to UXOs and damaged roads, SARC is leveraging local partnerships and alternative transport methods to deliver aid. However, funding gaps remain a critical concern, threatening the continuity of life-saving interventions. This comprehensive response highlights SARC’s commitment to immediate relief and early recovery, ensuring vulnerable communities receive dignified, inclusive, and timely assistance. lt/pgt
